title: See the Hostility Behind the Friendly Façade: The Law of Aggression

chapterBreakdown.gentle: The chapter on aggression stays useful because it names a pattern people often feel before they can explain it. This law argues that aggression often hides behind friendliness, delay, ambiguity, moral pose, or passive resistance, which makes sophisticated aggression more dangerous than open conflict. The sophistication matters because indirect aggression stays harder to confront. The aggressor can deny intent, call you oversensitive, or hide behind procedure and politeness. That forces the target to spend energy proving that anything is happening at all. The practical move is to see the pattern early, stop asking friendliness to cancel recurrence, set firmer boundaries, document behavior, and when necessary meet force with controlled aggression of your own: directness, firmness, and proportional consequence without loss of composure.
